q: Who is responsible to produce the record drawings?
n: Record drawings are also known as as-built drawings. The contractor produces record (as-built) drawings that show the work as actually constructed. The architect may review them. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 301 (General Conditions – Record Drawings); Architect's Guidelines (2016).

q: Where is a pipe sleeve typically required?
n: Pipe sleeves are cast into slabs and walls where pipes pass through. They allow movement and replacement, and penetrations can then be firestopped. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code (Sleeves); ASTM E814 (Firestop Systems).

q: Which construction method involves creating a reinforced concrete wall by excavating a trench stabilized with slurry before pouring concrete?
n: A slurry wall is formed by excavating a trench supported with bentonite slurry, then replacing the slurry with concrete. It is ideal for deep excavations, especially in urban settings, to manage groundwater and soil pressure. A slurry (diaphragm) wall is cast in a trench excavated under bentonite slurry, which holds the trench open until concrete is tremied in. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering (Diaphragm Walls); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 3.

q: In prestressed concrete, what method is used to offset or counteract the weight of the structure using the force from tendons?
n: Load balancing uses the force from prestressed tendons to counter the structure’s own weight, helping reduce deflection and improve performance. In the load-balancing method of prestressed concrete design, draped tendons exert upward forces that counteract part of the gravity load. Source: Lin & Burns, Design of Prestressed Concrete Structures (Load Balancing); Nawy, Prestressed Concrete.

q: Minimum main rebars for a spiral column.
n: Spirally reinforced columns need at least 6 longitudinal bars. Tied rectangular columns need 4. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 410.7.3.1 (Minimum number of longitudinal bars); ACI 318.

q: What is an ideal task lighting on the kitchen counter?
n: Under-cabinet strip lighting puts light right on the counter without shadows from the user's head. It is the ideal kitchen task lighting. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (Residential Kitchen Lighting).

q: Which of the following is considered a safety lighting?
n: Twin-head emergency lamps are battery-backed units that switch on automatically during power failure to light egress paths, so they are safety lighting. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR (Emergency Lighting); NFPA 101, Sec. 7.9.

q: Where should a UFO emergency light be installed?
n: UFO-type (round, recessed or surface) emergency lights are installed on the ceiling to spread egress illumination widely. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR (Emergency Lighting); manufacturers' installation guides.

q: Outline specifications are a deliverable under what design phase?
n: Outline specifications are part of the Design Development Phase deliverables, together with the developed drawings and the updated cost estimate. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Design Development Phase deliverables.

q: Which of the following BFP-issued documents is required for the building permit?
n: A Fire Safety Evaluation Clearance (FSEC) from the BFP is a prerequisite for the building permit. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR, Rule 9 (FSEC).

q: Which of the following BFP-issued documents is required for the occupancy permit?
n: A Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (FSIC) from the BFP is required for the certificate of occupancy and for business permits. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR, Rule 9 (FSIC).

q: Ideal type of door for closing and opening a commercial space unit.
n: A sectional (overhead) door closes a commercial unit securely. It opens upward in panels and needs no swing space. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 8 (Overhead Doors); DASMA standards.

q: Standared wind speed used in commercial air curtains.
n: Commercial air curtains typically discharge air at about 9–11 m/s at the nozzle, enough to keep a seal across the doorway. Source: AMCA 220 (Air Curtain Units – Laboratory Methods of Testing); manufacturers' data.

q: A 1.20m diameter circular table can accommodate how many seats?
n: A round table about 1.20 m in diameter seats 4 comfortably, and up to 6 at about 600 mm per person. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space (Dining); Neufert, Architects' Data.

q: Which construction system is most suitable for a manufacturing facility requiring fast construction, cost efficiency, and wide clear spans?
n: The PEB (Pre-Engineered Building) system is ideal for manufacturing facilities because it allows quick erection, reduced material waste, and large column-free spaces, making it more efficient than traditional systems like CIP (Cast-In-Place) or RCMF (Reinforced Concrete Moment Frame). Pre-engineered buildings (PEB) use factory-made steel frames and cladding that are bolted together quickly. They give wide clear spans at low cost, which suits factories and warehouses. Source: Allen & Iano, Fundamentals of Building Construction, Ch. 11 (Pre-engineered Metal Buildings); MBMA Metal Building Systems Manual.

q: What is the main advantage of a portal frame in low-rise buildings?
n: Portal frames have rigid beam-to-column joints, so they span widely without interior columns. That is the main reason they are used for low-rise sheds and halls. Source: Ching, Building Structures Illustrated (Rigid Frames); Schodek & Bechthold, Structures.

q: What is the connection point called where members meet in a space truss?
n: In a space truss, the members meet at nodes: spherical or plate connectors that join many members. Source: Schodek & Bechthold, Structures (Space Frames); Ching, Building Structures Illustrated.

q: Which document outlines the legal framework, common areas, and management rules for a small residential development or condominium project?
n: The master deed establishes the overall legal structure of the project, including common areas, unit boundaries, and management provisions, making it essential for the operation of residential developments or condominiums. The master deed (with its declaration of restrictions) establishes a condominium. It defines the units, the common areas and the management rules. Source: RA 4726 (Condominium Act), Sec. 4; PD 957 IRR.

q: Where within a residential lot is xeriscaping most ideally located?
n: Xeriscaping is most ideally located in the front yard, where it enhances curb appeal and conserves water by using drought-tolerant plants in the most exposed and publicly visible area of the property. Xeriscaping (drought-tolerant landscaping) is often placed in the front yard, where it adds curb appeal and saves the most irrigation water. Source: US EPA WaterSense (Xeriscaping); Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Site.

q: In the computation of plumbing fees, one ____ is composed of 1 WC, 2 FD, 1 LAV, 1 sink, 3 faucets and 1 shower head.
n: For plumbing permit fees, one "unit" is 1 water closet, 2 floor drains, 1 lavatory, 1 sink, 3 faucets and 1 shower head. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule II – Schedule of Fees (Plumbing Permit Fees).

q: Where is the best location for a lanai?
n: A lanai at the northeast corner gets morning sun and the cooler northeast breezes, and is shaded from the hot afternoon sun. Source: Koenigsberger et al., Manual of Tropical Housing and Building (Orientation); PAGASA climate data.

q: What type of Portland Cement is ideal for massive concrete construction?
n: Type IV (low-heat) Portland cement generates the least heat of hydration. That limits thermal cracking in massive pours such as dams and thick foundations. Source: ASTM C150 (Portland Cement Types); Kosmatka et al., Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures (PCA).

q: What concrete class is used for columns and slabs?
n: Structural members such as columns, beams and suspended slabs commonly use Class A concrete (1:2:4, about 21 MPa). Source: Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Concrete Classes); DPWH Standard Specifications, Item 405.

q: A rope used to control a lifted load's swing or rotation during lifting.
n: A tag line is a rope attached to a lifted load to help ground personnel guide, control, or stabilize it, especially in windy or tight conditions where the load might rotate or sway. A tag line is a rope tied to a suspended load. A worker uses it to control swing and rotation during lifting. Source: DOLE OSHS (Construction Safety – Rigging); ASME B30.5 (Mobile Cranes).

q: What shall be the bend diameter if the rebar size is 16mm?
n: For 10mm to 25mm rebars, the bend diameter shall be 6 times the bar diameter. Therefore, for 16mm rebar the bend diameter shall be 96mm or 4 inches. Standard hooks on bars from 10 mm through 25 mm need an inside bend diameter of 6 bar diameters. For 16 mm that is 6 × 16 = 96 mm, about 4 in. Source: NSCP 2015, Table 425.3.1 (Minimum Inside Bend Diameters); ACI 318.

q: In pitched-roof construction, what is the horizontal member that connects opposing rafters at their base to prevent them from spreading apart?
n: A tie beam is a horizontal structural member at the base of a roof truss or rafter set, designed to resist outward thrust and maintain the stability of the roof structure. In pitched roofs, the tie beam (or ceiling joist) joins the feet of opposing rafters. It holds them in tension so they cannot spread. Collar ties sit higher up. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 6 (Rafter Framing).

q: Which of the following is a volume quantity?
n: Building bulk is a volume, the three-dimensional envelope a building may occupy. OFB, development controls and BHL are faces, rules or heights. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII (Building Bulk and Building Envelope).

q: Which test is conducted on-site to determine the optimal moisture content and maximum dry density of soil for compaction purposes?
n: The Proctor test measures how well soil compacts at various moisture levels, helping ensure a stable base for construction. It is essential in site development for roads, foundations, and backfill areas. The Proctor compaction test finds a soil's optimum moisture content and maximum dry density. That sets the target for field compaction. Source: ASTM D698 / D1557 (Standard and Modified Proctor); Das, Principles of Geotechnical Engineering.

q: What is the primary purpose of using hub and tack in site development?
o: To serve as erosion control points
To indicate precise reference points for layout
n: Hub and tack are used to establish exact reference points for elevation, alignment, and location during construction layout, ensuring accurate transfer of plans onto the site. Hubs (stakes) with tacks driven into their tops mark precise survey reference points for setting out the layout. Source: Brinker & Wolf, Elementary Surveying (Construction Staking); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 1.

q: In a CARI policy, who is theinsurer who assumes the financial risk in case of loss or damage during the construction period?
n: Under a Contractor's All Risk Insurance (CARI) policy, the insurer, the insurance company, assumes the financial risk of loss or damage during construction. Source: Insurance Code of the Philippines (PD 612 as amended by RA 10607); UAP SPP Doc. 301 (Insurance).

q: What is the main basis for determining payment amounts in a construction progress billing?
n: The schedule of values is a detailed cost breakdown of a construction project, serving as the primary reference for calculating payments based on the percentage of work completed during each billing cycle. Progress billings are based on the schedule of values, which breaks the contract sum into work items. Payment is based on the percentage completed on each item. Source: AIA G702/G703 (Application and Certificate for Payment); UAP SPP Doc. 301.

q: Which of the following is an example of a floating floor system that uses interlocking edges for installation without adhesive or mechanical fasteners?
n: Click-lock flooring is designed with interlocking edges that snap together, allowing it to float above the subfloor without glue or fasteners. Click-lock flooring (laminate, engineered or vinyl) has interlocking edges that snap together. It floats on the underlay without glue or nails. Source: NWFA Installation Guidelines (Floating Floors); manufacturers' installation guides.

q: Which type of tile features patterns made by inlaid colors rather than surface glaze?
n: Encaustic tiles are made by layering different colors of clay into patterns, resulting in designs that won't wear off over time. Encaustic tiles get their pattern from colored clays inlaid into the body, not from a surface glaze. The pattern lasts as the tile wears. Source: Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction (Encaustic Tile); TCNA Handbook.

q: Why was popcorn ceiling originally used in residential construction?
o: To hide imperfections and absorb sound
To make ceilings easier to clean
n: Popcorn ceilings or stipple ceiling were popular for their ability to conceal surface flaws and provide sound dampening, reducing the need for perfectly smooth finishes and improving acoustic performance. Popcorn (acoustic) ceiling texture was sprayed on to hide surface defects cheaply and to absorb some sound. Source: Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction (Acoustic Ceiling Texture); US EPA (asbestos-era popcorn ceilings).

q: What is the standard projection of kitchen countertop lip?
n: Countertops commonly overhang the cabinet face by about 1 to 1.5 in, with 1.25 in typical. That protects the cabinet doors from drips. Source: NKBA Kitchen Planning Guidelines; Architectural Woodwork Standards (AWI, Countertops).

q: Which of the following spaces typically requires the use of cement backer board behind wall tiles?
n: Backer board is used in wet areas like showers to provide a moisture-resistant and stable surface for tile installation, preventing water damage and mold growth behind the tiles. Shower areas need cement backer board behind the tiles. Unlike gypsum board, it does not deteriorate when wet. Source: TCNA Handbook (Wet Area Installations); ANSI A118.9 (Cementitious Backer Units).

q: Which of the following areas have non-variable occupancy?
n: Per the exam key, the lobby is treated as a space of non-variable (continuous) occupancy for ventilation. Source: ASHRAE Standard 62.1 (Occupancy Categories); Philippine Green Building Code (2015).

q: What is a key benefit of passive design?
n: Passive design uses orientation, shading, daylighting and natural ventilation to cut the need for mechanical cooling and lighting. The result is lower energy use. Source: Lechner, Heating, Cooling, Lighting; Philippine Green Building Code (2015).
